title: CW: Q signals and prosigns
idea: A CW contact runs on short codes. Know what each one asks or says, how to match the other station's frequency and speed, and what full break-in means.

items: Is this frequency in use? (Are you busy?)
Go ahead, only the station I am working
Full break-in: receive between dots and dashes
Match your transmit frequency to the received signal

compare.how: Go ahead, only the station I am working.

traps.wrong: Breaking stations send the Morse code prosign “BK”
traps.why: BK is just a prosign for breaking in. QSK is the radio receiving between your dots and dashes.
QRS is about speed, not frequency.
Closing down is SK (or CL). KN means only the station I am working, go ahead.

traps.wrong: The fastest speed at which you are comfortable copying, but no slower than the CQ
traps.why: Backwards: never answer faster than the CQ. Slower is fine.

traps.wrong: Matching the speed of the transmitting station
traps.why: Zero beat is about frequency, not speed.
Key clicks are a K. C is chirp.
SK ends the contact. AR ends a formal message.

traps.wrong: We have already confirmed the contact
traps.why: QSL means received and understood, though QSL cards confirm contacts.
Send more slowly is QRS. QRN is static.
QRV is I am ready to receive.
